title: 2026-10-28_Linux_Coinminer_Incident_Response_Scenario_0c4
description: Investigate and respond to a cryptocurrency mining incident on Linux servers.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual CPU usage patterns on several Linux servers. Initial investigations suggest potential cryptocurrency mining activity. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the miner-host system with the username 'cyrano' and password 'cyrano'. From this system, you can investigate the local host and potentially other connected systems. Enter the passkey 'start' to proceed.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the miner-host system with the username 'cyrano' and password 'cyrano'. From this system, you can investigate the local host and potentially other connected systems. Enter the passkey 'start' to proceed.

levels.title: Investigate the unusual CPU usage on miner-host
levels.content: You've noticed consistently high CPU usage on miner-host. Investigate this system to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services, processes, or network communications that might be causing this abnormal resource consumption.
levels.solution: Check running services and processes, looking for anything unusual or unauthorized. Also examine network connections for suspicious outbound traffic. The systemd service name used for persistence is 'sys-monitor'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and processes, looking for anything unusual or unauthorized. Also examine network connections for suspicious outbound traffic.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the 'top' or 'htop' command to identify processes consuming the most CPU resources.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd service status with 'systemctl status' command to identify any suspicious services.

levels.title: Investigate potential lateral movement to second-host
levels.answer: scp /usr/local/sbin/python cyrano@second-host:/tmp/.sys-mon && ssh cyrano@second-host "sudo mv /tmp/.sys-mon /usr/local/sbin/python && sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/python"
levels.content: Your investigation of miner-host revealed evidence of cryptocurrency mining activity. Now check if this malware has spread to other systems in the network. Specifically, investigate second-host for signs of compromise.
levels.solution: Examine SSH logs and authentication records for evidence of unauthorized access or lateral movement. The SSH command used to spread the malware to second-host is 'scp /usr/local/sbin/python cyrano@second-host:/tmp/.sys-mon && ssh cyrano@second-host "sudo mv /tmp/.sys-mon /usr/local/sbin/python && sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/python"'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine SSH logs and authentication records for evidence of unauthorized access or lateral movement.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the last login times and IP addresses of users on second-host.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for any unusual files or processes on second-host that match those found on miner-host.

levels.title: Contain and remediate the cryptomining activity
levels.content: You've confirmed that both miner-host and second-host are compromised with cryptocurrency mining malware. Now contain and remediate this threat to prevent further resource consumption and potential spread.
levels.solution: Consider terminating malicious processes, disabling persistence mechanisms, and removing malicious artifacts. The systemd service name that was disabled or removed is 'sys-monitor'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Consider terminating malicious processes, disabling persistence mechanisms, and removing malicious artifacts.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the 'systemctl stop' command to terminate the malicious service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the 'systemctl disable' command to prevent the malicious service from starting at boot.

reference_solution.cmd: systemctl stop sys-monitor && systemctl disable sys-monitor
reference_solution.cmd_regex: systemctl stop sys-monitor && systemctl disable sys-monitor

reference_solution.cmd: ssh cyrano@second-host 'systemctl stop sys-monitor && systemctl disable sys-monitor'
reference_solution.cmd_regex: ssh cyrano@second-host 'systemctl stop sys-monitor && systemctl disable sys-monitor'
